content.source_title: Objective evidence of cardiac structural, functional and serological abnormalities consistent with left ventricular diastolic dysfunction/raised left ventricular filling pressures (Table 9)
content.summary_note: The greater the number of abnormalities present, the higher the likelihood of HFpEF.

parameters.Threshold: >34 mL/m^2 (sinus rhythm); threshold >40 mL/m^2 in atrial fibrillation
parameters.Comments: In the absence of AF or valve disease, LA enlargement reflects chronically elevated LV filling pressure.
Sensitivity 78%, specificity 59% for presence of HFpEF by invasive exercise testing. A higher cut-off of 13 had lower sensitivity (46%) but higher specificity (86%).
Up to 20% of patients with invasively proven HFpEF have natriuretic peptides below diagnostic thresholds, particularly in the presence of obesity.
See NT-proBNP comment regarding false negatives in some patients (eg obesity).

parameters.Parameter: PA systolic pressure / TR velocity at rest
parameters.Comments: Sensitivity 54%, specificity 85% for presence of HFpEF by invasive exercise testing.

parameters.Parameter: LV mass index / Relative wall thickness
parameters.Threshold: LV mass index ≥95 g/m^2 (female), ≥115 g/m^2 (male); relative wall thickness >0.42
parameters.Comments: Concentric LV remodelling or hypertrophy is supportive of HFpEF, but absence of LV hypertrophy does not exclude the diagnosis.
